newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan militia takes town from rebels, paper says.
newsitem.headline: Sudan militia takes town from rebels, paper says.

text.p: An official newspaper said on Monday that a militia allied with Sudan's government had recaptured the town of Akon from the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).

Al-Anbaa newspaper quoted Kerubino Kwanyin Bol, leader of the SPLA-Bahr al-Ghazal group, as saying his forces "seized the strategic town of Akon" in Aweil province, killing five SPLA soldiers, taking two prisoner and sending over 200 fleeing.
It did not say when the town was captured. There was no independent confirmation and SPLA officials were not immediately available for comment.

"The forces of the SPLA-Bahr al-Ghazal sector have continued their military campaign aimed at purging the areas of Bahr al-Ghazal of forces of (John) Garang's movement," al-Anbaa quoted Bol as saying, referring to the SPLA's leader.

Bol's group broke away from the mainstream SPLA several years ago and in April joined other factions in signing a peace accord with the government, now allied in the unified pro-government Southern Sudan Defense Force.
Garang has refused to sign the accord, saying the Islamist government in Khartoum is not serious about peace.
